jb2b4: An abstract color theory mural with pixellated gradients of color mapped to a Roman block wall. The work is a contemporary example of abstract Impressionism and is inspired by the early video game and graphics development of Chicago's history (Midway Games et al). The work features smooth, pixellated color gradients which depict the flow of water and the reversal of the flow of the Chicago River, as well as a large, abstract "Irish Eye" to commemorate the Irish immigrants who died reversing the flow of the Chicago River in this historically Irish Bridgeport riverfront location. The mural also features ancient geometries found in Chicago's historic brick facades and in Mitla, Oaxaca, Mexico---the artist's nod to the Mexican heritage of the Pilsen neighborhood it faces.
d6kfs: As human beings we are responsible for many of today’s problems. What we have done to the environment and Global Warming are addressed in this mural. Instead of focusing on the negative, the focus is going to be placed on a positive message. Even though we have been the cause of many of the problems, the most wonderful thing is we can also be the fix. Through the power of love, faith, hope and our intelligence we are capable of so many amazing things. Healing the earth and a better tomorrow can be two of those amazing things. It is my plan with this mural to remind the viewer of this and ask them to be part of the cure. With a lighthearted approach the animals of the earth are there to remind us that it is time to take action.
